root_cause.text: The xe DRM driver incorrectly relied on xe->info.probe_display being finalized by intel_display_device_probe() and failed to clear it when intel_display_device_info_runtime_init() later detected fuse-disabled display hardware, causing suspend/shutdown paths to run display code on uninitialized mode_config/cleared display state.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that “display may also be disabled via fuses, detected at a later time in intel_display_device_info_runtime_init()” and that in this case “the xe driver does for_each_intel_crtc() on uninitialized mode config in xe_display_flush_cleanup_work(), leading to a NULL pointer dereference”; the patch fixes this by calling intel_display_device_info_runtime_init() earlier and then checking intel_display_device_present(), setting xe->info.probe_display = false and unset_display_features(xe) when no display is present.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize display runtime info early and skip further display setup when runtime detection shows the display device is not present.
intent_record.what: The change inserts a call to intel_display_device_info_runtime_init(display) after intel_display_driver_early_probe(display), then adds a conditional check for !intel_display_device_present(display) that clears xe->info.probe_display, calls unset_display_features(xe), and returns 0 before continuing to intel_opregion_setup(display).
intent_record.how: At runtime, display device information is now initialized earlier, and if that initialization determines the display is not present or has been disabled, the function exits early after disabling display probing state and related features. This prevents the remaining early display initialization from running on a non-present display device.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove runtime display device info initialization from xe_display_init_early() to fix incorrect early initialization ordering in the display probe path.
intent_record.what: The call to intel_display_device_info_runtime_init(display); was removed from xe_display_init_early() after intel_bw_init_hw(display) and before intel_display_driver_probe_noirq(display).
intent_record.how: At runtime, xe_display_init_early() no longer performs display device info runtime initialization at that point in the early display setup sequence, leaving that initialization to occur elsewhere or not at all in this path, which changes the initialization order and avoids duplicate or misplaced setup during early probe.

grouping_result.intent: Initialize display runtime info early and skip further display setup when runtime detection shows the display device is not present.
Remove runtime display device info initialization from xe_display_init_early() to fix incorrect early initialization ordering in the display probe path.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by performing runtime display detection early and skipping display setup when the hardware is fuse-disabled/not present, preventing later paths from assuming probe_display remains valid and from running display code on uninitialized state.

The vulnerability is caused by incorrect display probe/initialization ordering and reliance on probe_display before runtime display info finalization. Removing runtime display device info initialization from xe_display_init_early() directly addresses that ordering problem in the display probe path.

candidates.rationale: This runtime detection was performed too late in the probe path. The root cause states the driver relied on probe_display being finalized earlier and failed to clear/act on it before later display setup, allowing display code to proceed even when runtime fuse detection disabled display hardware.

Because runtime display presence detection had not been handled early enough, this statement could continue into display probe/setup using state that should have been skipped when the display was fuse-disabled, contributing directly to uninitialized display state exposure.

This early display setup was executed before runtime detection could conclusively determine that display hardware was absent, matching the root cause of running display-related code on a device whose display state should have been considered unavailable.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement continues the display probe/setup path before runtime display detection has been handled early enough. When fuse-disabled hardware is only detected later, this call can leave display-related state partially or incorrectly initialized, leading later suspend/shutdown paths to run display code on invalid state.

This display-specific setup ran before runtime detection could establish that display hardware was actually unavailable. That matches the root cause of executing display initialization on systems where display should have been treated as absent.

This runtime display detection occurred too late in the initialization sequence. By relying on probe_display being effectively finalized only here, earlier and subsequent display setup could proceed on fuse-disabled hardware without clearing or acting on the disabled-display condition in time.
